answer: Every identity stakes a bond on one knoll, a hill that yields nectar only while its ember stays lit. The ember is a short-lived receipt, rekindled each epoch by a proof salted to its address, so no proof can be copied or parallelized. Each knoll is grouped by funding root: if one knoll in a cluster is proven fake, every bond in that cluster slashes by the square of the cluster size, so N clones sharing one root lose roughly N squared while one honest agent risks a single bond. As one root funds a second knoll, nectar thins, so a farm's yield per clone falls while its risk grows quadratically.
